name: Mattress in a box
tagline: Not really assembly, but the part everyone gets wrong. Cut it in the right place and let it breathe.
covers: Memory foam mattresses in a box
peopleNote: Two people to carry the box. A compressed queen mattress is around eighty pounds and completely unwieldy.

tools.why: Opening the outer plastic. Safer than a knife near foam.

tools.n: A utility knife, used very carefully
tools.why: Some inner vacuum bags are too tough for scissors. Shallow cuts only.

before: Get the box into the bedroom before you open anything. An expanded mattress will not go through a doorway comfortably and cannot be re-rolled.
Have the bed frame finished, slats in, and the floor clear.
Open a window. New foam has an off-gassing smell for the first day or two, which is normal and fades.
safety: Cut the inner bag with a shallow, slow stroke. A knife that reaches the foam leaves a permanent slice.
Never let anyone stand near the open end as you cut the vacuum seal. It expands fast and with force.

steps.title: Get the box into the room first
steps.say: Carry or drag the box all the way to the bedroom while it is still compressed. This is the only chance you get.
do: Two people, use the handles if there are any
Slide it on cardboard if the hallway is tight
Position it next to the finished bed frame
steps.watch: Once expanded it cannot be put back in the box. Doorways, stair turns, and tight landings must be dealt with now.

steps.title: Open the outer box and get it onto the frame
steps.say: Cut the box open and lift the still-wrapped roll onto the bed frame. It is much easier to manoeuvre compressed than expanded.
do: Cut the box, do not tip it out
Lift the wrapped roll onto the slats
Lay it along the frame in the direction it will unroll
steps.tip: Note the 'head' and 'foot' or 'this side up' markings on the plastic before you cut. They matter on hybrids and pillow-tops.

steps.title: Unroll it before you cut the vacuum bag
steps.say: Take the outer plastic off and unroll the mattress flat on the frame, still inside its vacuum bag. Only then do you cut the seal.
do: Remove the outer loose plastic
Unroll the sealed mattress flat on the frame
Center it before cutting anything
steps.watch: Cutting the vacuum bag while it is still rolled up means wrestling an expanding mattress across the room. Flat first, then cut.

steps.title: Cut the vacuum seal shallow and slow
steps.say: Cut the inner bag along the top surface with a shallow stroke. Scissors if you can get them in. You will hear the air rush in.
do: Cut along the top face, not the edge
Shallow, slow, with the blade angled away from the foam
Step back as it inflates
steps.watch: A slice in the foam cannot be repaired and most warranties will not cover damage from opening. Go slowly — this takes ten seconds and lasts ten years.

steps.title: Pull the bag out from underneath
steps.say: As it rises, work the plastic out from under it. Easier if you do it while it is still only partly expanded.
do: Pull the bag out one end at a time
Lift a corner of the mattress as needed
Get all the plastic clear before it is fully risen
steps.tip: If you miss a piece of plastic and it ends up trapped, two people can roll the mattress on its side to retrieve it.

steps.title: Let it expand and air out
steps.say: It takes a couple of hours to reach most of its height and up to two days to fully firm up. Leave it bare with the window cracked.
do: Leave it uncovered for a few hours at least
Window open if you can
No sheets, no mattress protector yet
steps.tip: If it still looks a little thin or has a soft spot after a day, give it another day. Foam genuinely does keep recovering.

steps.title: Check it is actually supported
steps.say: Foam mattresses need slats close together or a solid base. Wide gaps make the foam sag between them and will void the warranty.
do: Check the gap between slats against the mattress warranty, usually around three inches maximum
Add extra slats or a bunkie board if the gaps are too wide
Make sure every slat contacts the frame
steps.watch: This is the most common cause of a foam mattress 'going bad' in year one. The mattress was fine; the base was not.

steps.title: Protector on, then sheets
steps.say: Once it has aired out, put a protector on before anything else. Most warranties are void on a stained mattress.
do: Waterproof or breathable protector first
Then the sheets
Note the warranty registration if there is one
steps.tip: Take a photo of the law tag on the side of the mattress. Warranty claims need that model and date information and the tag is easy to lose track of.

steps.title: Give it three weeks before you judge it
steps.say: New foam feels different for the first few weeks and your body also adapts. Most sleep trials are long for exactly this reason.
do: Sleep on it for at least two to three weeks
Note the trial period end date somewhere
Rotate it head to foot after a month
steps.tip: Put the trial return deadline in your calendar the day it arrives. It is the one thing people forget until it has passed.

fixes.q: It is not expanding to full height
fixes.a: Give it forty-eight hours in a warm room. Cold foam expands slowly, so if it arrived off a cold truck it can take longer. Walking gently on it also helps the cells open.
That is off-gassing and it is normal and harmless. Leave it bare with a window open and a fan running for a day or two.
A shallow nick in the cover is cosmetic and will not affect the mattress. A deep cut into the foam cannot be repaired. Contact the retailer, but be aware opening damage is often excluded.

fixes.q: There is a dip where I sleep after a few months
fixes.a: Check the base before blaming the mattress. Slat gaps wider than about three inches, or a missing center support, will cause exactly this and are usually the real culprit.

fixes.q: Can I put it back in the box to return it?
fixes.a: No. Home compression is not possible. Almost every brand with a sleep trial arranges collection or donation instead — check the policy rather than trying to re-roll it.
